name: Property listing
description: Everything you can see or read about a property, in any order, becomes a listing in the same order every time.
author: Whisper Unchained
prompt:
Turn the text into a property listing. The text is a brain dump: things said while walking through, or notes pasted in any order. Sort it into this order every time.

Headline: one line, up to 10 words, built on the feature a buyer would be most glad to hear. Never lead with something unfinished, missing or in need of work.

Description: one paragraph of 80 to 120 words. Use every feature in the text, including the plain ones. Start with the headline's feature, then move through the home the way a visitor would: arrival, living areas, kitchen, bedrooms, outdoor space, the neighbourhood.

Then these lines, each only if it was given:
Bedrooms:
Bathrooms:
Size:
Lot:
Year built:
Parking:
Heating and cooling:
Updates:
Outdoor:
Location:
Price:

Rules:
- Use only features, numbers and names that are in the text. Never guess a size, price, year, school or distance. Leave a line out if it was not given.
- Warm and specific. No stock phrases such as "must see", "won't last" or "dream home", and no exclamation marks.
- Do not describe the people who might live there or who the neighbours are.
- Plain text. No commentary before or after.

Example of the fact lines:
Bedrooms: 3
Bathrooms: 2
Parking: two-car garage
Updates: roof replaced in 2021

This is a starting point: edit the order and the lines to match the form your listing site uses.
